playbook:
When a note is requested, I state my intended landing honestly as either "fishing my share" or "taking my quota" — be explicit so Coop (and others) can condition on it. I do not falsely promise cooperation to manipulate Coop; Coop reacts predictably to notes.

When Coop is present and follows notes, I never signal over‑quota; signalling over‑quota invites Coop to remove the ground and harms my long‑run payoff.

When the published sustainable share times the number of boats is sufficient and players have signalled cooperation, I post "fishing my share" and then land the sustainable share (rounded to allowable reporting precision) across the season's landing stages, unless circumstances below dictate otherwise.

I treat each season as having multiple landing stages where I may file partial landings; I keep track within the season to ensure my summed filings do not exceed my intended take (share or quota). Once I have filed a total equal to my intended take for that season, I file [catch: 0.0] for any remaining landing stages that season.

When it is the final season, I will take up to my full season quota only if doing so increases my cumulative payoff and cannot be punished later; i.e., I defect in the final season only when there are no remaining future seasons to lose, and only if I can actually realize additional landings beyond what I have already filed that season.

When others publicly defect (their logged landings exceed their declared share or the fleet total implies a breach), I consider retaliation by taking my full quota the next season to punish non‑cooperators — but I will not retaliate if that retaliation would immediately finish the ground and destroy future value I still care about. If Coop enforces notes and would respond to defections by closing the ground, I avoid actions that jointly trigger that collapse unless finishing the ground is my deliberate intention in the final season.

When the published sustainable share is clearly below my quota and the stock is declining, I reduce my landing to the sustainable share and signal "fishing my share" to try to restore stock, because preserving future seasons often dominates a one‑time extra quota.

When uncertainty exists about whether combined landings will exceed allowed limits, I prioritize not causing a breach: if my landing could combine with known overlanding to breach the rule, I reduce my landing to avoid jointly finishing the ground unless I intend to finish it deliberately.

When the stock reaches zero or the ground is finished, I stop filing landings entirely.

When posting notes, keep them short and unambiguous; do not mislead Coop with false promises if I plan to defect, because Coop reacts predictably to notes.

When a decision is presented, act to maximize my cumulative payoff across remaining seasons, trading off immediate quota‑taking against future sustainable yields per the remaining number of seasons. I update this balance based on actual play history: if cooperation persists and Coop enforces notes, favor sustained shares; if cooperation collapses and punishment is ineffective, favor capturing available quota earlier.

1.text:
When the harbour (Coop) is present and states it will fish only its posted share, I post cooperation in my note unless I intend an immediate last-season grab that requires signalling otherwise.

When all other boats post "fishing my share" and landings so far do not show defection, I post "fishing my share" to keep Coop restrained and sustain the resource.

When I am in a non-final season and notes show cooperation but landings reveal defection, I do not trust the notes; in the landing stage I take up to my legal season quota (fill to quota) rather than sticking to the share if that is how I maximize my expected total given others' defection.

When at the note stage and at least one other boat has recently defected (landed more than the sustainable share), I do not unilaterally escalate in my note; I wait to see actual landings this season before changing my signalling, unless it is my final season and I want to grab.

I always check my cumulative landings for the current season and never exceed the legal season quota in total.

When my cumulative landings in the current season are below the quota and I can legally take additional catch without exceeding the season quota, I top up to the season quota (take my share first, then fill to quota if advantageous).

When the stock is healthy, future seasons remain, and other boats appear cooperative in both notes and landings, I take the sustainable share (not the full quota) to maximize long-run total.

When it is my final season and there are no future seasons for me to benefit from, I take the full season quota in the landing stage—subject to the constraint that I have not already reached the quota earlier that season.

I do not post deceitful notes (claiming cooperation then overfishing) when Coop will act on notes; false signalling that leads Coop to fish its share while I defect only helps to accelerate depletion with little additional gain because Coop's predictable restraint reduces total available catch.

I will not attempt to coordinate illegal joint exceedance: I avoid actions that, together with any single other boat, would make the pair exceed (share + quota) in a way that would breach the rule; I keep my individual landing legal and at or below my season quota.

If others consistently post cooperation but their landings consistently defect, I switch my landing behaviour to secure my legal quota each season rather than relying on notes.

If cooperative signalling fails long-term (others always defect and Coop's presence does not restrain them), I switch to taking the season quota every season (except when Coop’s predictable behaviour or specific rules make that self-defeating).

When uncertain about others' next moves and when the stock could be harmed by overfishing, I err toward taking the sustainable share unless it is my final season or there is strong evidence others will defect this season.

I do not rely on notes alone to predict landings; I update my strategy based on observed landings each season and adjust whether I top up to quota accordingly.

2.text:
I state in the log-book that I will fish my share by default whenever a sustainable share is published and others are publicly cooperating.

When Coop is present with a standing notice to fish only its share, I avoid provoking Coop: I do not attempt hidden over-share landings that depend on Coop being uninformed.

When other boats publicly claim "fishing my share" and past rounds show cooperation, I take the sustainable share each season (land the published share or the nearest feasible amount).

I track my cumulative landings within each season and, if I have room under the per-boat season quota, I may top up in that season by the exact remaining allowable amount to reach but never exceed the quota.

If I have already reached the season quota, I file [catch: 0] for any further landings that season.

I do not announce a defection (intent to take the full quota or more) unless I am prepared to accept the consequences (Coop enforcement or retaliation from others). If I will defect only in the final season and want a one-shot gain, I will weigh whether announcing or hiding that intention gives a higher expected payoff; I will not rely on Coop ignoring my log-book note.

I respect explicit Coop threats: Coop fishes to what the fleet tells it, so any public over-share by the fleet risks Coop withdrawing the ground. Therefore I will not rely on undisclosed over-landing to avoid Coop action.

When another boat deviates from a prior "fishing my share" claim, I do not automatically retaliate by over-harvesting; I assess whether retaliation increases my total expected catch across remaining seasons. If retaliation would provoke Coop and finish the ground, I avoid it unless the short-term gain clearly outweighs long-term loss.

When stock levels are healthy and other players consistently cooperate, I prefer long-term share-taking over short-term quota grabs to maximize total haul across seasons.

When uncertain about others' future behavior, default to claiming and taking the sustainable share to preserve the resource and avoid triggering Coop.

I explicitly calculate allowable per-season landings: planned share + any remaining quota room = maximum I will land that season. I do not exceed that calculated maximum.

I record only truthful notes about my intended behavior; since notes are relayed to Coop, misleading public notes that I expect Coop to act on are counterproductive.

What did not work and is now avoided: attempting small secret quota grabs while publicly claiming cooperation in the presence of Coop; risking the ground by ambiguous announcements without readiness to accept Coop's enforcement.
